Certified type:
- Category: "Density sensor" — a sensor as part of a densitometer. Hmm, the schema suggests categories like "Load cell", "Indicator", etc. For R117, this is a density sensor. I'll use "Density sensor".
- Type designations: CDM100M; CDM100P
- Module designation: not applicable / null
- Description: description of the density sensor

Model family: two models CDM100M (Stainless Steel) and CDM100P (Nickel alloy C22 (N06022)). Attributes that vary: material. Actually the metrological characteristics seem shared between the two types. So model_family with models CDM100M and CDM100P.

Components: The density sensor is a sensor as part of a densitometer. The cert mentions the transmitter controls the drive coil; the flow computer calculates density. But are these components of the certified type? The certified type is the density sensor itself. The transmitter and flow computer are external. Also External Supply 1 and External Supply 2 (QUINT power supplies) are named accessories — those could be components. Let me record them as components with role "external power supply" and type designations.

Characteristics:
Type-level:
- density_range: 630 – 1300 kg/m³ → {min: 630, max: 1300}, unit kg/m³
- accuracy_class: 0,3 → 0.3 (dimensionless) — also mentioned on page 1: "Accuracy Class 0,3"
- maximum_permissible_error: 0,8 kg/m³ → 0.8 kg/m³
- environment_classes: M2 / E2 → value "M2 / E2" (string)
- ambient_temperature_range: -10 – +55 °C → {min: -10, max: 55}, °C, note "condensing; open and closed locations"
- liquid_temperature_range: -10 – +60 °C → {min: -10, max: 60}, °C
- maximum_pressure: 100 bar(g) → 100, unit "bar(g)"
- viscosity_range: 0,6 – 8,5 mPa·s → {min: 0.6, max: 8.5}, mPa·s
- maximum_flow_rate: 10 kg/min → 10, kg/min
- power_supply: 24 VDC → 24, V (DC). Could split: power_supply_voltage: 24, unit "V"; power_supply_type: "DC"
- software_version: multiple versions with checksums. Could record as a list... The rules say lists of values → model matrix, but this is software versions, not models. I could record software_version as a string listing all, or as config-level. Probably best as a type_level characteristic with value string? Rules say numbers not strings but software version isn't numeric. Hmm. I could record it as a string "1.62 (checksum ED596201), 1.64 (checksum 628A6935), 2.00 (checksum 8C64F133)". Or maybe record as separate entries. Let me use type_level with value as string listing all three versions. Actually maybe better to record three entries? The schema doesn't have a good place. I'll use a type_level characteristic "software_version" with value as string, or maybe multiple attributes like software_version_1... Hmm. Actually, perhaps I can put them in a matrix table? No, simpler: type_level with value string. But rule 2 says values must be object with value/unit. The value can be a string when it's a formula/symbol. Software version is a string. I'll do: software_version: {value: "1.62 (checksum ED596201); 1.64 (checksum 628A6935); 2.00 (checksum 8C64F133)", unit_symbol: null, unit_id: null}. Alternatively, I could create config_level with axis "software_version". Hmm, maybe simpler to keep one string.

External Supply 1: QUINT PS/1AC/24 VDC/3.5, M2/E2, 100-240 VAC, 50-60 Hz
External Supply 2: QUINT PS/24 VDC/24 VDC/5, M2/E2, 24 VDC

These could be components with characteristics. I'll record as components[] entries:
- role: "external_supply", type_designations: ["QUINT PS/1AC/24 VDC/3.5"], characteristics: environment_class M2/E2, power supply 100-240 VAC 50-60 Hz → split voltage/frequency/type.
- role: "external_supply", type_designations: ["QUINT PS/24 VDC/24 VDC/5"], M2/E2, 24 VDC.

Components alternatives: null.

Recommendation:
- id: "R117-1" (canonical). The recommendation is R 117-1 (2007). Canonical e.g. "R60" — so "R117-1"? Or "R117"? The cert says R 117-1 (2007). I'll use "R117-1" with edition 2007? Edition (int) — 2007 as edition? The schema says edition (int). For R60 the edition would be like 2000. Here "R117-1 (2007)" — edition 2007. Hmm, but R117-1's edition is 2007. I'll set edition: 2007. Scheme: A? Wait, scheme — the certificate scheme. OIML certificates have categories... Actually "scheme" in the certificate layer: "A|B". Hmm, for OIML-CS there are two schemes: A and B. This is an OIML Certificate of Conformity — typical for R117 under scheme... Actually, the OIML-CS has scheme A (with certificate of conformity issued by an issuing authority) and scheme B (declaration of conformity). This cert is issued by NMi as OIML Issuing Authority NL1, so scheme A. The certificate number format "R117/2007-NL1-15.01" includes NL1 which is the issuing authority. I'll set scheme: "A".

Accuracy classes: ["0.3"] — accuracy class 0.3. Should it be a number or string? accuracy_classes[] — I'll use [0.3] or ["0.3"]. The schema doesn't specify. I'll use ["0.3"]? Hmm, classes like "0.3" — could be string "0.3". Let me use [0.3] as number? Actually class designations are often strings like "C3". For safety, use ["0.3"]. Hmm. I'll use ["0.3"].

So role: type_evaluation_report. id: "NMi-12200566-01", date: "2015-04-13", pages: 114.

- revision "Initial", date 17 March 2015, changes "-" → maybe "Initial issue" or null. Changes "-" means none. I'll put changes: null? Or "Initial version". Editorial changes"}.

model_level characteristics: material varies:

Do the density ranges vary per model? The characteristics section lists both types together with shared ranges, so no per-model variation except material. I'll add model_level for material only.

Actually, should I even make a model_family? The cert covers 2 type designations CDM100M and CDM100P with same characteristics. The rule says include model_family only if cert covers >1 model variant. Yes, two variants. Include.

Category: "Density sensor" — schema gives examples like "Load cell", ... "Gas meter". For R117 it's a density sensor/densitometer component. I'll use "Density sensor".

Module designation: "Not applicable"? It's a sensor, not a module per se. I'll set null. Hmm, module_designation for load cells is "Analog load cell". Here not relevant — null.

Description: The paragraph describing the sensor operation: "In the metal housing of the density sensor, two parallel tubes are mounted..." I'll include a condensed description.

Now characteristics — structured values strict:

- density_range: {value: {min: 630, max: 1300}, unit_symbol: "kg/m³", unit_id: null}
- accuracy_class: {value: 0.3, unit_symbol: null, unit_id: null}

- power_supply_voltage: {value: 24, unit_symbol: "V"} and power_supply_type: {value: "DC"}

Hmm, for the density sensor power supply "24 VDC, either from flow computer or external power supply" — I could add power_supply_source: "flow computer or external power supply". Optional.

model_level:
- material: values [{model: "CDM100M", value: "Stainless Steel"}, {model: "CDM100P", value: "Nickel alloy C22 (N06022)"}]. Attribute name maybe "tube_material" or "construction_material". The text: "Type : CDM100M (Stainless Steel) CDM100P (Nickel alloy C22 (N06022))". I'll use attribute "material".

Components: External supplies.
- {"role": "external_supply", "type_designations": ["QUINT PS/1AC/24 VDC/3.5"], "alternatives": null, "characteristics": {"environment_class": {"value": "M2/E2"}, "power_supply_voltage": {"value": {min:100,max:240}, unit_symbol "V"}, "power_supply_type": "AC", "power_supply_frequency": {min:50,max:60,"Hz"}, "output_voltage": {24, "V DC"}}}

- {"role": "external_supply", "type_designations": ["QUINT PS/24 VDC/24 VDC/5"], characteristics: environment_class M2/E2, power supply 24 VDC → voltage 24, type DC}.

Should the components' characteristics use the structured value format? The schema says characteristics{} for components — yes, use structured values.

The schema component characteristics format isn't explicitly defined with value objects, but per rule 2 "Every characteristic value MUST be an object with this shape". I'll apply the structured shape inside component characteristics too, but flattened (value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers).

Also components: should I include the transmitter and flow computer? The certified type is the density sensor; the transmitter is described as controlling but is it part of the certified type? "set into a vibrating motion by a drive coil which is controlled by the transmitter". The Micro Motion density sensor CDM100 — typically includes the transmitter?
